Create a Field Book trait file

Source: R/trait_template.R
trait_template.Rd

Makes trait definitions for offline import into the Field Book Android app. Use phenotype_template() with no trait columns for the companion field CSV. No connection to Breedbase is needed to create either file.

Usage

trait_template(
  traits,
  format = "numeric",
  default_value = "",
  minimum = NA_real_,
  maximum = NA_real_,
  details = "",
  categories = "",
  is_visible = TRUE,
  output_file = NULL
)

Arguments

traits

Character vector of unique trait names. Use names that Breedbase can resolve when uploading observations later.

format

Field Book format: "numeric", "categorical", "percent", "date", "boolean", "text", "photo", "counter", "location", or "angle". A single value is repeated for all traits.

default_value, minimum, maximum, details

Optional defaults, numeric bounds and descriptions, respectively. Each must have length one or the number of traits. NA becomes an empty cell. Units can be included in details.

categories

For categorical traits, a character vector of slash-separated choices, or a list of character vectors, one per trait (e.g. list(character(), c("low", "medium", "high"))). A single value or list element is repeated. Other formats must leave this empty.

is_visible

Logical; show the trait in Field Book's Collect screen. Length one or the number of traits.

output_file

Optional path to a .trt file. Written as UTF-8 CSV with empty missing cells and no row names.

Value

A tibble with trait, format, defaultValue, minimum, maximum, details, categories, isVisible, and realPosition. The table is also returned when output_file is supplied.

Details

The columns follow Field Book's bundled sample trait file. Import the resulting .trt through Traits > Import/Export in the app. See the Field Book trait documentation. These local definitions do not create ontology traits in Breedbase; those must already exist before observations can be saved there.

See also

phenotype_template(), save_breedbase_phenotypes()

Examples

traits <- trait_template(
  c("fresh root yield", "notes"), format = c("numeric", "text"),
  minimum = c(0, NA), details = c("Yield in t/ha", "Field observations")
)
trait_template("severity", format = "categorical",
               categories = list(c("low", "medium", "high")))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   trait    format      defaultValue minimum maximum details categories isVisible
#>   <chr>    <chr>       <chr>        <chr>   <chr>   <chr>   <chr>      <chr>    
#> 1 severity categorical ""           ""      ""      ""      low/mediu… true     
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: realPosition <int>
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".trt")
trait_template("fresh root yield", minimum = 0, output_file = path)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   trait         format defaultValue minimum maximum details categories isVisible
#>   <chr>         <chr>  <chr>        <chr>   <chr>   <chr>   <chr>      <chr>    
#> 1 fresh root y… numer… ""           0       ""      ""      ""         true     
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: realPosition <int>
